sentences.text: 02. The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that:

On 15.11.2023 at about 07.00 a.m, the petitioner was driving his Goods vehicle bearing No. KA-16-D-5474 on the left side of Challakere to Parashurampura Road,
when he reached near Kaimara (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.601/2024 Gate, Air out, at that time the driver of Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-07-A-7845 drove his lorry in high speed, rash and negligent manner, came from opposite direction and dashed against the right side of the petitioner's vehicle.

Due to this the right hand of the petitioner was detached from his body and sustained grievous injuries and immediately he was shifted to Challakere Government hospital, wherein after necessary treatment and examinations the wounds are found and further he was shiftede to St. John's hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as inpatient from 15.11.2023 to 07.12.2023 and underwent surgery in the form of debridement and revision amputation of right upper limb, open reduction and internal fixation of IMIL Nail for femur fracture and other injuries were treated with necessary medications and discharged with an advice to take follow-up treatment regularly and has spent more than Rs.7,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges and he has to undergo one more surgery in future, for which he has to incur further medical expenses and prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 22 years and

was Driver by profession and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m. Due to the (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.601/2024 accidental injuries,
now he is bedridden and under treatment, due to which he is not able to do any work and suffering from permanent disability and also lost his marriage prospectus, which resulted in loss of income.

The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending Tipper Lorry involved in the accident and in this regard the Challakere Police have registered a case against driver of the said offending Tipper Lorry.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the RC Owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said offending Tipper Lorry, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a and costs.
03. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent, hence, was placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed written statement.

sentences.text:
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and contended that the offending vehicle had no permit at the time of accident and the alleged offending vehicle was used on public road without valid permit and there is a violation of policy terms and conditions (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.601/2024 and provisions of M.V. Act and admits that this respondent has issued a policy bearing No.431301/31/2024/1005 in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of Tipper Lorry bearing No. KA-07-A-7845 and their liability if any, is strictly in terms and conditions of the policy and provisions of M.V. Act and further contended that the driver of lorry did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drive the same at the time of accident and the owner has knowingly allowed the person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drive the same and there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy by the respondent No.1 and has further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the driver of the Tipper Lorry, age,
occupation, income of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive, exorbitant.

Hence,
pray for dismiss the petition against respondent No.2 with costs.

05. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following Issues:-
ISSUES 01. Whether the petitioner prove that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.601/2024 occurred on 15.11.2023 at about 07.00 a.m,
near Kaimara Gate, Air out, on Challakere Taluk, Chitradurga District, due to rash and negligent act of driving of the Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-07-A-7845 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
02 . Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03. What Order or Award?

06. The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and got examined doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability as PW.2 and through them got marked 19 documents as Ex.P.1 to 19 and closed the petitioner side evidence.
The respondent No.2 got examined its Administrative Officer and Superintendent, RTO as RW.1 and 2 and through them got marked 9 documents as Ex.R.1 to 9 and closed its side evidence.
07. I have heard the arguments advance by the learned counsels for the petitioner and respondent No.2 and perused the records.

REASONS 09. Issue No.1:- The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.
Though he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner.

During the course of cross- examination by the respondent No.2 counsel he denied to the suggestion that the accident was occurred due to his rash and negligent driving and not due to rash and negligent driving of the offending Tipper Lorry and also stated that he has not produced any document to show that he was earning Rs.30,000/- p.m by doing driving work.

10. Further, PW.2 is a Doctor, who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability of the petitioner, has stated that the petitioner sustained right arm traumatic amputation and fracture shaft femur right and he assessed permanent physical (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.601/2024 disability for right lower limb at 51% and permanent physical disability for right upper limb at 95% and further he stated that petitioner needs surgery for implant removal right femur and right trans humeral myoelectric prosthesis, which may cost approximately Rs.5,00,000/- and he has produced Disability assessment proforma, X-rays and X-ray report as per Ex.P.17 to 19.

During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.2 counsel he admits that before the petitioner came to his hospital, he is already undergone surgery for amputation right arm and admits that in the wound certificate femur fracture is not mentioned and he was taken complete treatment at St.John's hospital.

Fractures are united and he has assessed disability for particular limb and he has not assessed whole body disability and also stated that he has not issued any estimation regarding future medical expenses.
Petitioner can do his day to day work by using prosthesis with some difficulty.

12. On going through the oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner, the petitioner has clearly established and proved that the he sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.601/2024 15.11.2023 at about 07.00 a.m, on Challakere - Parashurampura Road, near Kaimara Gate, Air out, due to rash and negligent act of driving of Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-07-A-7845, by its driver as alleged in the petition.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Motor Vehicle Accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was aged about 22 years and was Driver by profession and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m and has spent more than Rs.7,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Due to the accidental injuries, he undergone pain and sufferings, loss of income, unable to do any work and has become permanent disabled.
14. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.
However he has produced Ex.P.10 Aadhaar card and Ex.P.11 Driving licence.

Eventhough the said documents are (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.601/2024 not authenticated documents for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of other evidence regarding his exact date of birth, the said documents can be relied upon and according to Ex.P.10 his date of birth is mentioned as 01.01.2001 and according to Ex.P.11 his date of birth is mentioned as 31.01.2001 and the alleged accident occurred on 15.11.2023.
Even taking into consideration of the said documents and Police records and medical records, it appears that as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner is 22 years.

Hence, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 22 years and as per the ratio laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and Others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 is 18.
15.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.16,000/-.

sentences.text: There is no doubt that the petitioner has sustained amputation of right arm.

For that a driver who has suffered a right arm amputation,
the percentage of functional disability is considered at 100%.
This is because the lost of the right arm significantly impacts their ability to perform the duties of a driver.
Driving a vehicle require the use of both hands for steering, operating controls, and potentially shifting gears.
Losing the right arm would make it impossible for the driver to safety operate the vehicle.
The amputation would render the individual unable to perform the function of a driver, meaning they would be unable to carryout their job duties.

In legal context, a 100% functional disability signifies that the individual has completely lost their ability to perform (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.601/2024 the activities associated with their profession or occupation, in this case, driving.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 100%.
Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:-
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.6 Discharge summary, according to which he was admitted in the hospital as inpatient totally for 23 days.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charge, special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.

18. Pain and sufferings:- As per Ex.P.7 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.2 doctor and as per medical records and X-ray and also sustained amputation of right arm, which indicates that on account of accidental injuries petitioner would have undergone pain and agony due to grievous injuries sustained.
Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.601/2024 suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.
19. Loss of income during laid up period:-

As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.16,000/- p.m and he has admitted in the hospital for 23 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast six months.
Thus, taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.96,000/- (Rs.16,000 x 6) under this head.
20. Medical expenses:- As per Ex.P.16 the petitioner has incurred medical expenses of Rs.3,17,463/-.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,17,463/- under the head of medical expenses.

21. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:- Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and amputation of right hand and fracture shaft femur right and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.601/2024 Rs.1,00,000/- towards future Anil Kumar vs Megha Engineering And Infrastructure on 28 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175305460/
6 loss of amenities and unhappiness.
22.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.45,69,463/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.1,00,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.

26. Regarding liability:- The respondent No.2 Insurance Company in its written statement has taken specific contention that as on the date of accident the offending tipper lorry has no Permit and hence, Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.601/2024 to the petitioner.
On behalf of the respondent No.2, its Administrative Officer is examined as RW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the written statement averments therein.

On going through the said documents and permit history extract, it is very much clear that earlier the offending lorry had permit valid from 20.09.2017 to 19.09.2022 and subsequently said permit was not renewed after it expiry and only on 13.12.2023 to 13.12.2028 permit was in force and it means as on the date of accident i.e., 15.11.2023 the permit was not renewed or permit was not in existence.

The respondent No.2 has relied upon the citation reported in No.3297/2019 (MV-D) in a case of Nadilakshmamma and others V/s Raju.B and another, wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that in a case of if driver had no driving licence, under such circumstances, it is held that Insurance Company cannot fastened liability of pay and recover when there is clearly breach of policy conditions and liability to pay compensation is on respondent No.1/owner himself.

It is further held that, the Insurance Company would not have issued the policy (SCCH-3) 23 M.V.C.No.601/2024 unless FC was in force and it appears that the FC expired after the issuance of policy.

37. In MFA 7391/2013 dt:28.06.2021 in a case of The Secretary, Bapuji Vidya Samsthe ,
Shivamogga V/s Umeshanaika and others, wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that insurer is liable even if the vehicle lacks FC, not having a valid FC was not a fundamental breach.
The main contention of this Insurance Company that inspite of no Permit to ply the vehicle in that place and no FC, the tribunal committed an error in fastening the liability.
The contention of the Insurance Company cannot be accepted.
If the insurance of a vehicle was valid as on the date of accident, then the liability of the Insurance Company cannot be obsolved even if there was no FC.

In the said decision it is further held in para 9 that, "In view of the Judgments of this Court in MFA No.6021/2006 (MV) dt:08.03.2010, MFA No.6311/2014 (MV) dt:02.12.2014 and MFA No.8573/2014 (MV) dt:02.09.2015, held that, even in the absence of Fitness Certificate, the Insurance Company cannot contend that they are not liable to pay the compensation when there was a contract of Insurance and the other policy conditions are fulfilled.

Hence, I am of the opinion that it requires interference of this Court and the Tribunal committed an error in fastening the liability on the appellant herein instead of fastening the liability on the Insurance Company.

Therefore, on the above said decision,
eventhough the vehicle had no FC and Permit, the insurer is held liable to pay compensation and recover it from the owner and driver.

Therefore, respondent No.1 being the RC owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle shall jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
